comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C36-C42 regarding MARCM clonal analysis. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED, with OpenEval emphasizing quantitative data strength and peer reviewers accepting the findings while noting phenotypes are weaker than other mutants.

Perfect agreement on claims C43-C48 regarding twin-spot RGT analysis of division outcomes. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes varying sample sizes and suggests mechanism could be more direct, while peer reviewers accept the findings without concerns.
Perfect agreement on claims C52-C53 regarding Numb asymmetric segregation. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED, treating this as confirmatory data consistent with prior literature (Sallé et al., 2017).

Perfect agreement on claims C11, C69-C74 regarding the mechanistic model. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the model is interpretive and speculative regarding molecular mechanisms, while peer reviewers accept it as a reasonable 'back up' protection mechanism interpretation.

Both address claims C3, C27-C32 regarding Put/Dl double RNAi and ligand-independent Notch activation. OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED, while peer review evaluates as UNCERTAIN due to Reviewer 2's concern about temporal depletion kinetics affecting interpretation of ligand independence.

Strong agreement on claims C56-C63 regarding bleomycin-induced regeneration revealing Numb requirement. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED with high confidence. OpenEval emphasizes differential effects of bleomycin vs DSS and large sample sizes, while peer reviewers describe this as demonstrating an essential role during regeneration.

Both address RNAi data showing genetic interaction (claims C8, C33-C35). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval also includes claims C4, C7, C9, C65, C79, C80 and mentions Figure 3 MARCM data, while peer review focuses specifically on the RNAi experiments without concerns.

Both address mild homeostatic phenotype of numb mutants (claims C49-C51). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval includes additional claims C6, C26, C37-C38, C64 and emphasizes BMP dominance, while peer review focuses on the moderate ISC loss phenotype.

Partial overlap on claims C4, C7, C65 regarding parallel pathway model interpretation. OpenEval evaluates experimental data as SUPPORTED, while peer review R7 evaluates the interpretive model itself as SUPPORTED, with reviewers accepting the 'back up' mechanism concept.

Minor overlap on claims C37-C38 regarding clone analysis. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval R5 focuses on mild phenotype under homeostasis, while peer R3 addresses the full MARCM clonal analysis dataset.

Minor overlap on claims C54-C55 regarding numb mutant phenotypes. OpenEval R6 evaluates regeneration context as SUPPORTED, while peer R5 evaluates homeostatic context as SUPPORTED, reflecting different experimental conditions.

OpenEval R9 addresses claims C1-C2, C12-C25 as established background knowledge from prior literature, evaluated as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers typically do not comment on background citations.

OpenEval R10 addresses claims C5, C75 regarding low Numb detectability from prior work (Goulas et al., 2012; Sallé et al., 2017), evaluated as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval R11 addresses claims C66-C68 regarding BMP fluctuation during regeneration from prior work (Tian et al., 2017), evaluated as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
